startup.name: Goodshelf
startup.one_liner: The online retailer for AI shopping agents
startup.description: AI native online retailer that sells curated products across electronics, home, travel, beauty and furniture, with structured product data, comparisons and evidence based recommendations for both human shoppers and AI assistants. Revenue would come from product sales margin and possibly brand partnerships. Team size is not given in the input (listed as 0), San Francisco, Winter 2025 batch.

yc_acceptance.basis: Starting prior is about 1 percent for a random applicant (0.6 to 2 percent, references/yc_acceptance.md). Down for a consumer retailer idea with no stated traction or technical wedge, since consumer and marketplace companies with no repeat usage are discounted in the factor table and defensibility is weak. Up slightly because agent facing commerce is a new angle and YC has funded e-commerce infrastructure. Net about 1.5 percent; the company is already in the batch so this is for completeness.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most likely say that online retail is a thin margin, inventory and logistics heavy business that Amazon and Walmart dominate, and that the claim that AI agents will buy through a new retailer is untested. Partners would ask why agents would prefer Goodshelf over Amazon, which already answers shopping questions with its own assistant, and where defensible advantage lies.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry Consumer --years 2022-2025 --calibration-only: seed cond 56% (n=16, lower 43 / upper 67), series_a cond 0% known (n=9, upper 24%). Narrow cohorts python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --tag E-commerce --years 2018-2025 --calibration-only: seed cond 85% (n=13), series_a cond 36% (n=11), series_b cond 50% (n=4); and --tag Marketplace: seed 79% (n=19), series_a cond 53% (n=15), series_b cond 25% (n=8). All three cohorts are under 30 companies, so they are anecdotes. Time table era 2022+: seed median 8 months from batch start; Consumer median 13 months (n=39); series_a median 28 months.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window is 22.4 months, from 2025-01-06 to 2026-11-17, and counts a round above about 1M from outside investors closing inside it. Anchor 0.56 for Consumer 2022 and later (n=16); the tiny E-commerce and Marketplace cohorts show 79 to 85 percent but are anecdotes. A 22 month window covers most eventual seeds, so 0.56 times about 0.85 is 0.48, then 0.40 after a discount for weak retail margins and no team data. 0.40 is 0.7x of the Consumer anchor. A hot AI commerce theme is not lifted above the anchor, per the winners test. These odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under 3M, typical for consumer e-commerce with modest early sales.
Institutional seed near the 2022 and later median of 3.5M to 4.1M if the agent traffic thesis shows early orders.
Strong seed if agent driven sales grow fast and a known fund backs the thesis; the 6M to 10M quartile is rare for retail.
Large seed only if the company becomes the reference shopping layer for assistants; very rare for a retailer.

ladder.why_it_fails: The seed step fails if orders from AI agents stay negligible and the company has to buy traffic like any small retailer, leaving thin gross margin and little to show investors. Adla (a department store for e-commerce) reached only a seed then shut down, and In Stock, Shopagram, PerShop and ShopWith all ended without strong rounds. Investors who fund retail want a differentiated supply or data advantage, which the description does not show.

bands.rationale: Small or slow Series A below the 2022 and later YC median of 14.15M (stage_benchmarks.md), led by the seed investor.
Typical Series A near the 2022 and later YC median of 14.15M with quartiles 10M and 20M.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A inside 22 months needs scaled sales with healthy gross margin, and retailers must show repeat purchase and manageable inventory risk. The failed retail analogs (Adla, ShopWith, Lalabox) raised seeds but could not reach an A, and consumer marketplaces in the data rarely scale without paid acquisition costs eating the margin.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Online retail has thin margins, high customer acquisition cost and strong incumbents, so most small retailers stall or shut down, as In Stock, Adla and PerShop did. A good outcome needs agents to send real purchase volume to the store, which is unproven.

killers.risk: AI agent driven purchases stay too small to support a retailer, and Amazon, Walmart and the model labs capture them
killers.evidence: Amazon launched its Rufus shopping assistant in 2024 and rolled it out to all US users in July 2024, so large retailers already own agentic shopping.
killers.mitigation: Win a narrow category where agents need structured data that big retailers lack and prove order volume.

killers.risk: Gross margin and inventory risk make the business capital heavy
killers.evidence: Retailers carry inventory, shipping and returns costs; PerShop and Adla could not turn curation into profit.
killers.mitigation: Use drop shipping and affiliate revenue before holding inventory.

killers.risk: Founders and team data are missing, so execution is unknown and the story reads as a thesis not a company
killers.evidence: The input lists team size as 0 and gives no traction numbers, only a mission statement.
killers.mitigation: Show orders and agent traffic, and name the founders' retail or data background.

technical_complexity.rationale: A structured product catalog and a store front are standard software and a small team can launch one in three months. The hard parts are supplier relationships, fulfilment, return handling and getting assistants to cite and route to the store, which is dependency on platforms the team does not control.

takeover_risk.rationale: Large retailers and assistant makers already add shopping features, and structured data is easy to copy. Goodshelf depends on the assistants that may also become the retailers' own channel, which gives limited defensibility.

evidence.claim: Amazon rolled out a generative shopping assistant to all US shoppers in July 2024, showing assistants in shopping are real, though owned by the incumbent
Amazon said Rufus answered tens of millions of questions soon after launch, evidence of shopper interest in assistant led shopping

roadmap.proof: Monthly sales above 100K with positive contribution margin
Gross margin above 30 percent and repeat orders above 30 percent

brand.name: Goodshelf
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Goodshelf" --era 2022+: kind invented_or_proper, length 9 to 11, 2 syllables; cohort alive 92.6 percent, exit 4.5 percent, no outlier.
weaknesses: Compound of common words, hard to trademark
brand.rationale: A compound of two common words suggests a curated shop, comparable to Wayfair or Shelf style names, and is memorable but not distinctive. It carries no effect on the ladder beyond ordinary brand recall.

narrative.headline: A thesis driven AI retailer against Amazon; a seed in 22 months is possible but retail margins and no team data hold it back.
narrative.general_summary: Goodshelf wants to be the store AI shopping agents buy from, a new angle on a business where past YC curated retailers such as Adla, In Stock and PerShop shut down. The Consumer cohort gives 56 percent seed ever, and a 22 month window captures most of that, so the estimate is 40 percent with a discount for retail margins and an unknown team. A Series A is a small tail. The odds do not rank this company against others.

assumptions: Team size is listed as 0 in the input, which is treated as unknown, not as a solo founder.
Window 22.4 months; seed means a round above about 1M from outside investors closing inside it.
E-commerce and Marketplace cohorts are under 30 researched companies and are used only as anecdotes.
